newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq capable of exporting 2.4/2.5 mln bpd - minister.
newsitem.headline: Iraq capable of exporting 2.4/2.5 mln bpd - minister.

text.p: Iraq is capable now of exporting up to 2.5 million barrels per day (bpd), Oil minister Amir Mohammed Rasheed said on Friday.
"We are capable today, and I mean today, of exporting approximately 2.4 to 2.5 million bpd," Rasheed told a news conference.
He said Iraq would need some spare parts and accessories to boost exports to three million bpd.
"Then within a certain other period, possibly a year, we could come to 3.5 to 3.6 million bpd," he said.
He said Iraq viewed its oil-for-food deal with the U.N. worth $2 billion over six months as a temporary measure which will eventually lead to a total lifting of curbs on its oil exports.
He put Iraq's refining capacity at 800,000 bpd of which Iraq was using only 580,000 to meet its domestic needs and those of Jordan.
He said Iraq was seeking help from international firms to complete a 150,000 bpd refinery, work on which began prior to the imposition of U.N. trade sanctions for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

He said deals with foreign firms to develop oilfields throughout Iraq were at "a very advanced stage." He said international firms had tentatively agreed to invest up to $20 billion in Iraq's oil industry and increase Iraq's output to six million bpd by the turn of the century.
Rasheed said French and Russian firms were in the forefront of international companies approaching Iraq and his country intended to give them preferential treatment.
He said Iraq also had a tentative contract with China's CNPC to develop Ahdab oilfield in the southeast. Ahdab has proven reserves of more than one billion barrels.
